subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence with correct parallel structure: To succeed, Lara must plan carefully, manage time, and ____.
explanation: Parallel structure requires same verb form: plan, manage, delegate. 'delegate tasks' matches the other base verbs.

subject: English Language
text: Which completes the sentence correctly? The bouquet of roses ____ on the windowsill.
explanation: The subject is the singular noun 'bouquet', so a singular verb 'is' is required (not plural 'were' or 'are').

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best completion: By the time she arrives, we ____ dinner.
explanation: 'By the time' with a future reference calls for the future perfect: 'will have finished' (completed before her arrival).

subject: English Language
text: Select the best word: His speech was so ____ that everyone followed his argument easily.
explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand; contrasts with 'verbose' (wordy) and 'tacit' (unspoken) or 'belligerent' (hostile).

subject: English Language
text: Complete with the appropriate idiom: She decided to ____ and apologize after the misunderstanding.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to face an unpleasant action bravely (here, apologize); other idioms have different meanings.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly punctuated and capitalised for this sentence: The director said "we begin production next Monday"
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
The director said, "We begin production next Monday."
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct punctuation: comma before the quotation, capitalise the first word inside quotes, and capitalise the day 'Monday'. Title 'director' is lower-case here.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'photography'?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
explanation: 'Photography' has primary stress on the second syllable: pho-TOG-ra-phy. Stress patterns differ from 'photograph' and 'photographer'.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with 'bough' (pronounced /baʊ/)?
explanation: 'Bough' has the diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'cow'. 'Though' and 'low' use /oʊ/; 'cough' uses /ɒf/ or /ɔf/.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: Would you mind closing the door, please?
explanation: 'Would you mind ... please?' is a conventional polite request form; others are direct, imperative, or confrontational.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best passive form: The committee will announce the results tomorrow.
options: The results will announce the committee tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
Tomorrow will the results be announced by committee.
By the committee the results will be announced tomorrow.
explanation: Correct passive: object becomes subject + 'will be announced' + 'by the committee' with normal word order; option 0 follows this pattern.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.
explanation: For unreal present conditional, English uses the subjunctive 'were' after 'If I ...', not 'was' or 'am'. 'Had been' suits past counterfactuals.

subject: English Language
text: After three failed sketches, Ada smiled and set a fresh sheet on the easel. What is most reasonably inferred?
options: Ada accepted that she could not sketch.
Ada sold her sketches to a gallery.
Ada prepared to start another attempt.
explanation: Placing a fresh sheet on the easel after failed attempts implies she intends to try again; it does not imply giving up or selling work.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the employees ____ aware of the new schedule.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'employees' (plural) requires 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By 8 p.m. tonight, I ____ the final draft.
explanation: Use the future perfect (will have + past participle) for an action completed before a specified future time.

subject: English Language
text: Her explanation was _____; no one misunderstood the process.
explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easily understood; contrasts with 'tacit' (implied), 'prosaic' (dull) and 'terse' (brief).

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: After the delay, they decided to ____ and start without the vendor.
explanation: 'Press on' means to continue or proceed despite obstacles; other idioms mean stop, sleep, or persist in a different sense.

subject: English Language
text: The essay title reads: "a study of market trends in West Africa". Which is correctly capitalised?
options: A Study of Market Trends in West Africa
The study of market trends in west africa
The stated rule does not apply in this context
Study Of Market Trends In West Africa
explanation: Title case capitalises principal words and proper nouns; 'A Study of Market Trends in West Africa' follows that rule.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in 'consequence'?
explanation: 'Consequence' has primary stress on the first syllable: CON-se-quence; primary stress marks the strongest syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'caught'?
explanation: In many accents 'caught' and 'court' share the /ɔː/ vowel; 'coat' and 'cart' have different vowel qualities, 'cot' differs in many varieties.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is an offer?
options: Do you mind if I open the window?
I can help you with the report.
explanation: 'I can help you...' is an offer of assistance. The others are requests or polite questions, not offers of help.

subject: English Language
text: Report: Clara said, 'I will attend the seminar tomorrow.' Which is the correct reported form?
options: Clara said that she would attend the seminar the following day.
Clara said that she will attend the seminar tomorrow.
Clara said that she attended the seminar tomorrow.
Clara said that she had attended the seminar tomorrow.
explanation: In reported speech, 'will' backshifts to 'would' and time expressions like 'tomorrow' change to 'the following day'.

subject: English Language
text: If only I ____ earlier, I would have caught the bus.
explanation: 'If only' with a past counterfactual requires the past perfect (had + past participle) to show an unreal past condition.

subject: English Language
text: The new policy requires staff to complete training, to submit a health form, and ____.
explanation: Maintain parallel infinitive form: 'to complete', 'to submit', 'to attend' — so 'attend an orientation' matches the structure.

subject: English Language
text: After reviewing the submitted forms, Mr. Bello rejected several because they lacked signatures. What is most reasonably inferred?
explanation: If forms lacked signatures, the reasonable inference is they were incomplete; other options are not directly supported by the statement.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the students nor the professor ____ present at the seminar.
explanation: With 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer noun; 'professor' is singular so use 'is'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time Olamide arrives, we ____ the minutes of the meeting.
explanation: Use the future perfect 'will have sent' for an action completed before a future reference point.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best word: His remark was so _____ that it offended the audience.
explanation: 'Inflammatory' means likely to provoke strong feeling or offence, unlike 'candid' (frank) or 'mundane' (dull).

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: After months of delay, the team decided to ____ and move forward.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept and get on with something difficult; other options mean avoid, cheat, or shift blame.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly punctuated and capitalised for this sentence: The museum guide said "we will close at Five O'clock."
options: The museum guide said, "We will close at five o'clock."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct form uses a comma before the quotation, initial capital inside quotes, and 'five o'clock' in lower-case; colons/semicolons are incorrect here.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'economics'?
explanation: Standard pronunciation places primary stress on the third syllable: ec-o-NOM-ics; stress contrasts identify word rhythm and meaning.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'put' (/pʊt/)?
explanation: 'Put' and 'foot' share the short /ʊ/ vowel; 'food' and 'boot' use /uː/ and 'putt' uses /ʌ/ in many accents.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following sentences is an apology?
explanation: An apology explicitly expresses regret; 'I apologise for arriving late' is a direct apology, others are request, statement, or offer.

subject: English Language
text: Change to reported speech: Lamina said, "I must finish the report by Monday."
options: Lamina said that she had to finish the report by Monday.
Lamina said that she must finish the report by Monday.
Lamina said she will finish the report by Monday.
Lamina said that she has to finish the report by Monday.
explanation: In reported speech, modal 'must' backshifts to 'had to' when original utterance is reported in past tense; other choices fail the standard backshift.

subject: English Language
text: If I ____ the map, we would not have gotten lost.
explanation: This third conditional requires a past perfect form in the if-clause: 'had read' + result clause referring to a past consequence.

subject: English Language
text: Which is correctly punctuated: After the heavy rain the roads were flooded.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
After the heavy rain, the roads were flooded.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: An introductory adverbial phrase should be followed by a comma: 'After the heavy rain, the roads were flooded.' Commas must not split noun phrases incorrectly.

subject: English Language
text: When the electricity failed during the presentation, the students improvised drawings on the blackboard.
options: They downloaded slides to their phones.
They postponed the session until power returned.
They continued the presentation using alternative visuals.
explanation: The most reasonable inference is they used the blackboard as an alternative visual aid to continue; other options contradict 'improvised drawings'.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence with correct parallel structure: The coach expects players to arrive on time, to attend practice, and ___.
explanation: Parallel structure requires identical grammatical forms in a list. Here all items use the infinitive form 'to ...', so 'to maintain discipline' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Every student, together with the prefects, ____ required to register.
explanation: The subject 'Every student' is singular; phrases like 'together with the prefects' do not change agreement. Use singular verb 'is'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the dean reads this report, we ____ it twice.
explanation: The future perfect ('will have' + past participle) denotes completion before a future point. 'Will have proofread' shows two completions before the dean reads it.

subject: English Language
text: His explanation was so laconic that the audience found it ____.
explanation: 'Laconic' means using few words; the closest synonym is 'brief'. 'Elaborate' and 'confusing' are opposites or irrelevant.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the idiom that means to accept a difficult decision: '____'.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept or endure an unpleasant decision. 'Spill the beans' means reveal a secret; others differ in meaning.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly punctuated and capitalised for this sentence: The lecturer said "we will retire the old textbooks next term".
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
The lecturer said, "We will retire the old textbooks next term."
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Standard punctuation: use a comma before a direct quotation, capitalise the first word inside the quote, and place the closing full stop inside the quotation marks.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'democracy'?
explanation: Pronunciation of 'democracy' is /dɪˈmɒkrəsi/ with primary stress on the second syllable 'moc'. Knowledge of stress patterns distinguishes correct choice.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'caught' (pronounced /kɔːt/)?
explanation: In standard British pronunciation 'caught' and 'bought' share the long /ɔː/ vowel. 'Cot', 'coat', and 'cut' use different vowel sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence represents an offer? 'Shall I carry your bag to the office?','Which is the speech function of this sentence?
explanation: 'Shall I carry your bag...?' proposes to do something for someone; that is an offer. A request would ask the person to do something themselves.

subject: English Language
text: Change to reported speech: Aisha said, 'I am writing the minutes now.'
options: Aisha said that she writes the minutes now.
Aisha said that she was writing the minutes then.
Aisha said she will be writing the minutes now.
Aisha said she had written the minutes then.
explanation: Present progressive in direct speech backshifts to past progressive in reported speech ('am writing' → 'was writing') and 'now' changes to 'then'.

subject: English Language
text: If the workshop _____ on Friday, many participants will attend.
explanation: First conditional uses present simple in the 'if' clause and 'will' in the main clause. 'If the workshop is held' is the correct present-simple protasis.

subject: English Language
text: After the meeting, Kemi locked the office and walked out, leaving her umbrella on the chair. What is most reasonably inferred?
options: She left the umbrella because she intended to return soon.
She lent the umbrella to a colleague.
She disposed of the umbrella before leaving.
She forgot to take her umbrella when she left.
explanation: Leaving the umbrella on the chair while locking up most reasonably suggests omission or forgetting; other options add assumptions not supported by the sentence.

subject: English Language
text: Select the sentence that completes the list in parallel: He promised to call, to visit, and ____.
options: that he would send a message
explanation: Parallel structure requires matching infinitive forms: 'to call, to visit, and to send a message' maintains the same verb form.

subject: English Language
text: Which is correct? A series of tests ____ necessary before graduation.
explanation: Collective noun 'a series' is treated as singular with singular verb: 'A series ... is necessary.'

subject: English Language
text: Complete: Before she returns from Lagos, we ____ the arrangements.
explanation: Future perfect ('will have completed') shows completion before a future time: before she returns.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best word: His explanation was so ____ that the committee understood the issue at once.
explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, contrasting with 'convoluted', 'opaque', and 'ambiguous'.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: After months of hesitation, Sade decided to bite the ____ and accept the job.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is the idiom meaning to face a difficult decision; other options are not idiomatic here.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly punctuated and capitalised for this sentence: the teacher announced "exams start next week"
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
The teacher announced, "Exams start next week."
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech begins with a capital and ends with terminal punctuation inside quotes: "Exams start next week."

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'restaurant'?
explanation: In standard English 'restaurant' has primary stress on the first syllable: RES-taurant.

subject: English Language
text: Which word ends with the same consonant sound as 'laugh' (/læf/)?
explanation: 'Laugh' and 'enough' end with the /f/ sound; 'though' ends /oʊ/, 'live' and 'have' end with voiced consonants.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following sentences is an offer?
options: I can lend you my umbrella.
Would you mind opening the window?
Do you know when the bus leaves?
explanation: An offer expresses readiness to give help or an item: 'I can lend you my umbrella' is an offer; others are request, apology, and question.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: 'They will publish the research next month.' Which is correct?
options: Next month will be published the research.
The research will be published next month.
The research will publish next month.
They will be published the research next month.
explanation: Passive form moves object to subject with appropriate be + past participle: 'The research will be published next month.'

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: Unless she ____ the application by Friday, it will not be considered.
explanation: Conditional 'Unless' with future consequence takes present simple in the if-clause: 'Unless she submits... it will not...'.

subject: English Language
text: Mini-passage: After rehearsal Musa left his music stand in the hall overnight. The next morning it was gone. What is most reasonably inferred?
options: Musa had taken the stand home earlier.
Musa sold the stand before rehearsal.
Someone moved or took the stand from the hall.
explanation: If the stand was left and then missing, the reasonable inference is that someone moved or took it; other choices contradict the given facts.
